about.what: Service catalogue of demo seed v1: ten categories and seventy jobs with the same keys in both configurations. Names, hours, parts, brands and prices are each market's own.
how_to_read: hours: standard hours of the job for vehicle class 'car' (US flat-rate hours / нормо-часы). hours_by_class multiplies them; null for a class means the job is not offered for it; a missing table means the hours do not depend on the class. On a menu-priced job the same multiplier applies to the price.

labour_price: list labour for class 'car' before and after the last price rise, and history: the price in each period of price_history.<cfg>.labour_hour, oldest first. hourly = hours x posted hour; menu = a fixed price that follows the hour only at a rise. labour_price_company is the company-account price class.

parts: one entry per part or fluid, with one option per tier (economy, standard, premium). A slot with a standard option only is the same in every tier. cost is the shop's purchase price, list_price what the customer pays, both for class 'car' and before tax. parts_scale_with_class: multiply by configurations.<cfg>.parts_class_multiplier.

shop_supplies: true when the job's labour counts toward the shop-supplies fee (hourly-priced jobs); the rate and the cap are in configurations.<cfg>.shop_supplies. fees are fixed charges of the job itself (tyre disposal, storage).
usually_sublet: true when the shop sends the work to a subcontractor; sublet then holds what is sent, its cost and the price to the customer, and hours cover only the shop's own removal and fitting.
an option with story: 'S6' is the cheap pad of story S6; the seeder uses it only where the story says, and the tier averages leave it out.

share_of_orders.lead: share of all orders on which the job is the reason for the visit (sums to 1 over the catalogue). addon: share of all orders on which it rides on another lead job. total = lead + addon = share of orders that carry the job.

recommended_share: of the times the job is sold, how often it came from an inspection finding instead of the customer's request. Summed over the jobs with share_of_orders.total it gives the recommended jobs sold per order at the company's sold share (ledger sold.company, mix.sold_rec_jobs_per_order).
counts_as_priced_job: false only for the free courtesy inspection, which is left out of the jobs-per-order count.
about.money: USD with cents; RUB whole, list prices rounded to 10. English prices are before sales tax; Russian prices, list and company-account, hold VAT from 2025-01-01 for every customer, an account billed on terms included: the price is what is paid and the amount before VAT is the price / 1.05 (ledger tax.ru_price_basis).

price_rise.when: P: the first Monday on or after T - 150 days (the last rise; ledger price.hour.history)
price_rise.applies_to: the posted labour hour, the company-account hour and every menu labour price
price_rise.not_applied_to: parts, fluids, fees and sublet prices: they follow purchase cost and did not move with the rise
price_rise.reading: the ledger's posted hour (135 USD, 1 900 RUB) is today's rate, after the last rise; before_rise is the rate before it. The Russian configuration had two earlier rises: see price_history

price_history.what: what a job cost on any date of the 24 months of history. Ledger rows: price.hour.history, price.hour.company_history, price.parts_drift_year, price.rise.last_pct

rule.hourly labour: hours x the hour in force on the order's date
rule.menu labour: today's menu price x the hour in force then / the hour today, rounded to cents (en) or to 10 RUB (ru); each job carries the result in labour_price.history
rule.parts, fluids, tyres, fees, sublet: from G to T (the product period) today's price; before G today's price x (1 - parts_drift_per_year) ^ years, where years = days before G / 365.25, rounded to cents (en) or to 10 RUB (ru); cost moves with list, so the margin holds. They did not move at a labour rise (ledger price.parts_drift_year)
rule.shop supplies: the rate and the cap are the same over the whole history
rule.company account: hourly work at the company-account hour of the same date; menu prices and parts at 10 % off the list price of the same date, not rounded again: cents (en) and kopecks (ru) are kept (ledger price.company_rounding)

labour_hour.from: the first open day on or after T-18 months
the first full open day on or after T-335 days

pn_status_legend.seen: the number was seen for this or a closely matching application on retailer listings found by web search on 2026-11-13 (search summaries of listings, not the brand's own catalogue)
pn_status_legend.recalled: written from memory as a real catalogue number of this brand for this application; not re-checked in this pass, so the number or its fitment may be off
pn_status_legend.styled: follows the brand's real numbering pattern but is not a checked catalogue number; never present it as a real one
pn_status_legend.none: no catalogue number: sold by description, size or by the litre
pn_status_legend.fictional: the brand does not exist; invented on purpose for story S6

company_account_terms.applies_to: the price class 'company account' of the labor_rate table, held by the two big accounts (A1, A2); the medium accounts and small business customers pay list
company_account_terms.basis: designed (X): a negotiated fleet rate 10 % under the posted hour and 10 % off parts list; menu-priced jobs take 10 % off the menu price

parts_margin.method: gross margin on list price: list = cost / (1 - margin)
parts_margin.basis: Ratchet+Wrench 2026 survey (us-shop.md): parts gross profit 50 to 59 % is the most common band (27 %), 40 to 49 % next (24 %). A cost matrix marks cheap parts up more than dear ones, so economy sits just above the band and premium just under it; tyres and batteries carry the trade's thin margins. The tier-weighted result is printed by the check.

shop_supplies.name: Shop supplies
shop_supplies.rule: 5 % of hourly-priced labour on the order, at most 35 USD; menu-priced jobs carry none

tax.on: parts, labour, fees and shop supplies
tax.note: ledger tax.rate.main, tax.rate.east, tax.rate.west: Chattanooga 9.25 %, Nashville 9.75 % for the whole of the bought shop's history; rate is the home shops'. Every price in this file is before tax

company_account_terms.applies_to: the price class 'company account' of the labor_rate table, held by the two big accounts (A1, A2); the medium accounts and small business customers pay list
company_account_terms.basis: designed (X): договорной нормо-час 1 700 руб. (about 10 % under the posted one) and 10 % off parts list; fixed-price jobs take 10 % off

parts_margin.method: markup on purchase price: list = cost x (1 + markup), rounded to 10 RUB
parts_margin.basis: designed (X), accepted range of the tier-weighted gross margin 25 to 35 %. No published figure exists: ru-shop.md lists parts margin as a gap, and the one trade voice found in this pass (business-gazeta.ru/article/552467, read as a search summary only) says the markup on dear parts starts at about 15 % and cheap parts carry more. Reasoning: the customer can look the retail price up online and may bring own parts, so the shop's list price sits at the online retail price and the shop keeps the wholesale discount: about 30 % markup on original and dear parts, 40 % on mainstream brands, 50 % on cheap ones, more on oil sold by the litre.

shop_supplies.name: Расходные материалы
shop_supplies.rule: 3 % of the hourly-priced work on the order, at most 500 RUB; fixed-price jobs carry none

tax.on: work, parts, fees and shop supplies on bills dated from 2025-01-01; none before
tax.note: ledger tax.ru_price_basis: a price in this file is what the customer pays, VAT inside from 2025-01-01, whoever the customer is: a private or small-business customer and A3 to A6 the list figure, A1 and A2 the company-account class. Nothing is added on top; the amount before VAT is the price / 1.05. An account's счёт and УПД show the amount before VAT, the VAT and the total as separate figures
